groups.description: Focused Hspec examples for the root package's console startup and exit integration.
Focused Hspec examples for the foundation package's Logging, Resources, Failures, Recovery, Workers, Messaging, and Time contracts.

Focused Hspec examples for the runtime package's application runner and lifecycle, logging lifetime, reporting, supervision, inbox services, package boundaries, resource smoke, and supervised messaging waits.

Headless Hspec examples for the GLFW package's session, window, command, control, host, dynamic window, monitor, input, and mode models over the test seam, its link declarations against the native manifest, and its package boundaries. Initializes no GLFW and needs no display.
Run the console executable's smoke mode end to end.

Focused Hspec examples for the Lua host package's fault and cancellation transport across the foreign-call boundary, stack and registry discipline, terminal close, independent execution under the threaded RTS, selectable standard libraries, and its export boundary. Runs the uninterruptible-Lua example in a child process.

The Linux confinement and resource-limit feasibility probe (LUA-14). Launches confined children through the candidate namespace, private-root, and seccomp profile; records the machine, the permissions, and whether the profile installed at all; and checks the fail-closed refusal, the denied native and Lua accesses with the mechanism that denied each, two-instance isolation and independent termination, the whole-process memory ceiling, the execution bound's escalation, and the three lifetime cases. Built and run on Linux only; on other platforms the components are not built. A green run is evidence, never a supported-platform verdict.

Portable Hspec contracts for the GPU retention and frame-ownership model: typed identities and the misuse they are rejected as, the hold ledger and disposal eligibility, frame ownership phases and their obligations, validated admission budgets and their backpressure, recovery and allocation-retry accounting, and bounded round-robin owner progress under a scripted clock. It runs through the CPU project and needs no Vulkan SDK.

Hspec examples driving the documentation landing helper, this planner, the CI image builder, the native recipe helper, and the isolated X11 display helper against temporary Git repositories, and the boundary that keeps the VK-2 Vulkan proof out of the mandatory floor and holds its compatibility summary to the records it quotes.
Real GLFW session, thread, and window examples through the shared native Hspec fixture, on an isolated X11 display.

LUA-15's local macOS feasibility proof: a confined helper's denied filesystem, network, process, and native-module accesses before and after its mod source loads, two-instance process and storage isolation, the enforced whole-process memory limit and the execution bound, and the three lifetime endings. Optional and Darwin-only; the component is not built elsewhere, so a request for it on Linux fails rather than passing vacuously.
